title: stream-client: ergonomics for reauth/backoff and connection pooling + version bump
author: Lina Moreno
description:
Context: The Go SDK's streaming client diverged from the Python/TS SDK ergonomics for reauthorization and retry/backoff behavior. Customers reported awkward token-refresh callbacks and brittle stream reconnect semantics during token rotation and transient infra errors (see ENG-1942). This PR consolidates the Go streaming surface to match cross-SDK patterns while adding a couple of Go-specific ergonomics (connection pooling and typed errors).

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces a StreamManager abstraction that centralizes: connection pooling, graceful reauth, and transparent resume semantics.
- Adds token-refresh hook APIs (Sync and Async variants) so callers can supply either a fast local refresh or an async refresh backed by a shared credential cache.
- Implements an adaptive backoff algorithm tuned for continuous-batching workloads (short-circuit for 4xx, exponential+jitter for 5xx/network).
- Surface typed StreamError values with Retryable()/Permanent() helpers for easier switch-case handling.
- Improves CI test coverage with deterministic stream-failure simulators and a new integration test that validates token rotation during an active stream.
- Updates documentation and examples.
- Bumps module minor version to v0.9.0 and updates CHANGELOG.

Motivation: Converge SDK UX across languages to reduce user confusion and enable cross-language examples in docs while keeping Go ergonomics idiomatic (context cancellation-first, explicit pool lifecycles).

Design notes:
- StreamManager: callers can opt-in to an internal connection pool or use a single-connection mode. Pool size defaults to min(4, GOMAXPROCS) and is configurable via WithStreamPool(size). The manager is responsible for re-establishing individual conn slices and reattaching KV-caches where supported.
- Reauth hooks: two interfaces added: TokenProvider (synchronous) and AsyncTokenProvider (returns channel/future). The streaming runtime prefers synchronous calls when possible to avoid head-of-line blocking. Async providers are polled with backpressure and a small prefetch window.
- Adaptive backoff: classifies errors into categories (ClientError, TransientServerError, NetworkError) and applies immediate retry for client-side rate-limit sparing (429 -> token-rotate signal), exponential backoff for server errors, and a fast-retry path for short-lived network blips. Tuned to keep tail latency < 200ms on local benchmarks.

Compatibility: Backwards compatible for existing users who do not opt into StreamManager. New APIs are additive and gated behind functional options. Some internal packages changed signatures; we kept deprecated shims with deprecation notes.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for backoff policy and StreamError types.
- [x] Integration test for token rotation mid-stream.
- [x] Documentation updates and example.
- [x] CHANGELOG entry and version bump.
- [x] Manual QA: streaming demo app tested against staging inference cluster.

Review summary and conversation: 
- Maya Chen: "High level: I like the StreamManager abstraction. Two asks: (1) expand comment on pool shutdown semantics to avoid leaking goroutines, (2) please add an end-to-end test that simulates a slow token provider causing head-of-line blocking."
- Lina (author): "Addressed both: added an explicit ShutdownWithCtx(ctx) call and a pooled worker that will early-abort if context is cancelled; added token_rotation_test that injects a 250ms latency token provider and asserts progress continues."
- Arjun Patel: "Adaptive backoff looks solid; please add a README note about 429 handling and when users should prefer token-rotation vs client-side throttling."
- Lina: "Added a short section in docs/streaming.md and a code example demonstrating 429 callback that triggers token refresh."
- Simone Kaur: "One nit: stream_error typed constants should live in errors package root. Otherwise LGTM."
- Lina: "Moved the constants and added an alias in internal/errors for backwards compatibility."

CI: Full CI passed after one flake rerun. New integration stage runs under a mocked inference endpoint with deterministic failure injection; one earlier run failed due to test timing (flaky), we increased timeouts and it's now stable.

Merge: Squash merge to main. Merge commit message includes a short summary and references ENG-1942 and ENG-1987.

Release notes: "Go SDK v0.9.0: StreamManager with connection pooling, adaptive backoff tuned for streaming workloads, reauth hooks for token rotation, typed stream errors, and improved integration tests. Backwards compatible defaults. See docs/streaming.md for migration notes."

Breaking change: "false"
